title: Game Design
description:
One artifact covering scope, session, retention, monetization, progression and economy.

These are NOT separate stages and not separate documents. Scope depends on monetization, which depends on session, which depends on scope — sequencing them invents an order that does not exist, and splitting them into four files guarantees they drift apart. One artifact with a recorded consistency result is atomic; four files cannot be.

The `consistency` block is what makes 'these were co-designed' checkable rather than asserted. It is produced by evaluating core/reference/design-consistency-rules.yaml and is the exit guard on title:design.

The human-readable GDD is a RENDERING of this artifact (see core/templates/gdd.md), not a separate source of truth.

Schema 1.1.0 adds three optional blocks — `engine`, `features` and `build_spec` — which carry the design down to what an implementation agent needs to build the MVP without guessing. They are optional so 1.0.0 artifacts stay valid; the design module always emits them. Schema 1.7.0 adds `build_spec.depth`: the meta loop, goal ladder, content schedule, first-session length and return hooks, each tiered.

research.description: Research V2 (added in 1.8.0): the research this design was derived from, carried from the strategy, and `applied`: which design decisions (archetype, fantasy, identity kit, timing targets) came from research and which fell back to a default. Absent when the strategy carries no research.

brief.description: The game idea a person started the run with (`wgf new-game "..."`), verbatim in its canonical form: NFC, trimmed, whitespace runs as one space. Absent when the run was a blank market scan. Copied from the title-strategy. An agent author designs the game it describes; the built-in author fits the buildable concept research selected, and records in open_questions a dimension the brief names that the design does not use. Added in 1.4.0.

core_loop.description: The repeating unit of play, stated as a cycle. If it cannot be written as a loop, it is not one.

pillars.description: Two or three. More than three means none of them decide anything.

tiers.description: Explicit scope tiers. The factory must be able to say 'this feature is excluded because it does not contribute enough to initial validation' — and that sentence needs somewhere to live.

content_units.description: Countable content: levels, maps, enemy types, puzzle sets. The number the consistency rules check against session length.

progression_terminal.description: How progression ends, or an explicit statement that it loops. Open-ended progression is an endless content obligation.

session.description: Explicit because it is the thing most often left implicit and then contradicted by the monetization plan. Values depend on genre, audience, platform and monetization — there are no universal numbers, which is why none are defaulted here.

time_to_first_play_s.description: From load to the player doing something. Web portal traffic has no install cost anchoring it, so this is unforgiving.

structure.description: How a session begins, escalates and ends. A session that ends arbitrarily reads as being interrupted.

reward_moments_per_session.description: Natural points where the player wants something. Rewarded video only works at these, which is why the consistency rules check it.

return_reason.description: Why a player opens this again tomorrow, in their words rather than in mechanics.

monetization.description: Designed before production, not retrofitted. Platform-aware: game code calls the template's platform abstraction, never a portal SDK directly.

trigger.description: The in-game moment. 'On death, offer a continue' — not 'every 90 seconds'.

player_value.description: What the player gets. Required thinking for rewarded placements: if the answer is nothing, it is an interstitial wearing a costume.

asset_requirements.description: The assets the design needs, by kind. The asset manifest is built from this list; when it is absent a baseline is derived from screens, audio direction and locales, which is a floor, not a design. Kinds are the keys of core/reference/asset-policy.yaml.

source.description: The intended final source. Absent means library first, then procedural.

tags.description: Words a library search matches on.

width.description: Logical width: layout pixels, before `scale`. For a spritesheet, one frame.

frames.description: For a spritesheet or an animation.

scale.description: The resolution the pixels are authored at: 2 means twice the logical size in pixels, drawn at the logical size. Default 1.

atlas.description: An atlas group. Sprites, UI, icons and VFX naming the same group are packed into one texture atlas; group what is drawn together (one scene, one HUD).

animations.description: A spritesheet's named animations. Absent: one looping animation, named after the asset, over every frame.

frames.description: Frame indices into the sheet, or frame names. Absent: every frame.

tile_width.description: For a tileset: logical tile width. Default 32.

existing.description: An asset already chosen, with where it came from. Its license and origin are checked like any other external asset's.

path.description: Relative to the game repository root.

atlas.description: For a spritesheet: its atlas descriptor, relative to the repository root. Default: <stem>.atlas.json, then <stem>.json.

model.description: For model, environment and animation kinds: the asset as data. With parts it is built headless into a GLB; always, what it declares (clips, LODs, collision proxy, fitted size, budget) is checked against the delivered file.

platform_constraints_applied.description: Which binding platform requirements this design absorbed, and how. Populated from the pinned platform profiles. An empty list on a title with required platforms means the profiles were not read.

engine.description: The engine the design is drawn for: PixiJS or Phaser for 2D, Three.js for 3D. Recorded at design because dimensionality changes the asset list, the camera, the controls and the load budget — a design that does not know which it is cannot be costed. Which 2D engine is a smaller decision than the dimension, and `dimension: 2d` with no `type` means the 2D default; tech-plan owns the binding selection (`tech_plan.engine.type`, guard engine_selected) and must agree with this, or supersede the design.

rationale.description: Why this game needs this dimensionality. Load budget, asset pipeline cost and readability on a phone are rationales; 'looks better' is not.

camera.description: Fixed, follow, orbit, isometric… and what it frames.

features.description: Every feature of the game, tiered. The canonical tier list: scope.tiers is derived from it (mvp → mvp and prototype, post-mvp → production, optional → future), so the two cannot drift. An mvp feature carries acceptance criteria because the implementation agent builds against them, not against taste.

build_spec.description: What the implementation agent builds from. The prose fields above (core_loop, controls, progression, difficulty, ux, art_direction, audio_direction) are the summary a person reads; this is the specification a coding agent reads, and the MVP must be buildable from it without guessing. Every entry carries a tier. Ids are local to this artifact and cross-referenced within it (a screen names the game state it belongs to; a touchpoint names the state it fires in), which is what makes the spec checkable for dangling references. Platform capabilities are named generically — game code calls the template's platform abstraction, never a portal SDK.

rules.description: Testable statements. 'Feels good' is not a rule.

parameters.description: Starting tuning values, so the first build is playable rather than zeroed.

pause.description: How play pauses, including on tab blur and during an ad.

moment.description: What the player is trying to do in the next five seconds.

persistence.description: What is saved between sessions, and where.

assist.description: What happens for a player who keeps failing.

game_states.description: The game's own state machine — boot, loading, menu, play, pause, fail, results. Not the title lifecycle.

state.description: The game state this screen is shown in.

metric.description: The game metric this element displays (score, lives, moves...), named as build_spec.experience names it.

feedback.description: What the player sees and hears. A reward nobody notices is not one.

continue_offer.description: A monetization touchpoint id, when failure offers a continue.

session_flow.description: The session as an ordered sequence of beats, from page load to the natural stopping point.

state.description: The game state it is offered in.

when_unavailable.description: What the game does when the platform has no fill, no ads, or the player declines. Never a dead button.

required.description: Required by a platform profile, as opposed to chosen by the design.

fallback.description: Behaviour on a platform that lacks the capability.

assets.description: Asset REQUIREMENTS. The assets step turns them into the asset-manifest, with sources resolved and licences recorded.

role.description: What it is to the player. The entity roles are the play probe's (shared/play-probe.schema.json): an entity the probe reports with that role is drawn with this asset in production.

readability.description: What a first-time player must recognise in it, and at what size or distance: 'a goalkeeper in gloves, readable at 60 px tall from the play camera'. Production assets are judged against it.

scale_mode.description: fit letterboxes, fill crops, expand reveals more world.

resize.description: What happens on resize or rotation mid-play.

visual_identity.description: A deliberate look, specified so two implementers would build the same thing. Generic UI — system fonts, default purple gradients, evenly spread pastel palettes, rounded cards everywhere — is a design failure, not a neutral default.

source.description: Where the faces come from and their licence, since they ship in the bundle.

primitive_style.description: Present only when the art direction itself is geometric (an abstract neon runner): readable entities may then be drawn as primitives in production. Absent, a cube or sphere standing for a character is a placeholder, and the production gates refuse it.

ui.description: The UI's look, as numbers and palette tokens: what the production gate and visual QA hold the screens to.

min_target_px.description: Smallest interactive element on a phone viewport, CSS px.

button.description: fill and text are palette tokens.

surface.description: Palette token for panels and result cards.

experience.description: The player-experience contract: what a first-time player must be able to tell, and how fast - the objective and where it is shown, how play is won and lost, how every action is acknowledged, how the game teaches before it tests, and the first-30-seconds budget. Optional before 1.5.0; the design module requires it of every design it produces and checks it against core/reference/experience-rules.yaml and the rest of the build_spec.

statement.description: The objective, in the words the player is shown.

metric.description: The metric the objective is measured in; an MVP hud element shows it.

shown_on.description: The screen id that shows the statement before or as play starts.

win.description: Absent when play has no win: an endless run chases a best.

metric.description: The metric whose value ends play (lives, moves, time), when there is one.

actions.description: One entry per MVP control action: how the game acknowledges it.

visual.description: What changes on screen when the action is taken.

updates.description: Metrics the action changes; each is shown by an MVP hud element.

teaches.description: Control action ids the first session teaches before it tests them.

grace.description: A first-time player cannot fail before this.

reveals_answer.description: True when onboarding shows the player the correct move rather than teaching them to read it.

depth.description: Why a player plays longer and comes back: the loop above the run and what it persists, a goal at every horizon, content-variety items introduced on a schedule, the first session's designed length, and the stated reasons to return. Every entry carries a tier, so depth the prototype does not build is visible as post-mvp or optional rather than claimed. `delivered_by` names what builds an entry (a feature, mechanic, progression step, reward or hud id); an mvp entry may only rest on an mvp one. Added in 1.7.0, optional in the schema; the design module requires it of every design it produces and checks it against core/reference/design-depth.yaml. Craft: core/craft/retention-and-progression.md.

statement.description: The loop across sessions as a cycle: play -> earn -> spend or unlock -> a reason to play again.

persists.description: What survives between sessions, each with its own tier.

goal_ladder.description: Goals at three horizons: short (seconds to a minute, inside a run), mid (this run or this session), long (across sessions).

measure.description: How reaching it is counted: a metric, a threshold.

content_schedule.description: Content-variety items the player meets over time, in the order they arrive. `at_s` is seconds into a run; `after_runs` is runs completed (or a stage reached) before it appears; `introduced` says when in words.

ends_on.description: The beat a first session is designed to end on, and what the player leaves wanting.

statement.description: The reason, in the player's words.

consistency.description: The recorded result of evaluating core/reference/design-consistency-rules.yaml. Exit guard on title:design.

warnings_acknowledged.description: Set at G3. A warning nobody read is just a comment.

open_questions.description: Things the prototype is expected to answer. Better recorded than silently assumed.

tier.description: mvp: built before prototype review, and what the prototype is judged on. post-mvp: production, after G4 passes. optional: a candidate for later, committed to nothing.

localId.description: An id local to this artifact, referenced from elsewhere inside it.
